43575.q: Roughly what share of the vote did the SVP achieve in its best National Council result so far (as of 2025)?
43575.e: The SVP achieved its best result in 2015 with 29.4 per cent. That is the highest share for any party since proportional representation was introduced.
43575.m: In 2015 the SVP won almost 30 per cent.

43576.q: Who was president of the SVP Switzerland from 2020 to 2024?
43576.e: Ticino member of the Council of States Marco Chiesa succeeded Albert Rösti in 2020. Under him, the SVP clearly won the 2023 elections.
43576.m: Marco Chiesa led the SVP from 2020 to 2024.

43577.q: How did the SVP react after the Federal Assembly did not re-elect Christoph Blocher to the Federal Council in December 2007?
a: It declared itself an opposition party
It demanded a new election of Parliament
43577.e: The SVP parliamentary group no longer regarded the two elected SVP members as its representatives and went into opposition. This phase only ended a year later with a new Federal Council election.
43577.m: After Blocher was voted out in 2007, the SVP went into opposition for about a year.

43578.q: With the election of which politician did the SVP officially return to the Federal Council in December 2008?
43578.e: Ueli Maurer was elected in December 2008 as successor to Samuel Schmid. This ended the SVP's role as opposition.
43578.m: Ueli Maurer brought the SVP back into the Federal Council in 2008.

43579.q: Which SVP popular initiative on the free movement of persons did the people and the cantons reject in September 2020?
43579.e: The Limitation Initiative wanted to end the free movement of persons with the EU. It was rejected on 27 September 2020 with about 62 per cent voting no.
43579.m: The SVP's Limitation Initiative failed at the ballot box in 2020.

43580.q: What was the SVP initiative rejected in 2018 that wanted to place Swiss law above international law as a rule called?
43580.e: The initiative “Swiss law instead of foreign judges” is known for short as the Self-Determination Initiative. The people and the cantons clearly rejected it in November 2018.
43580.m: The Self-Determination Initiative wanted to put national law above international law.

43581.q: Which cantonal party shaped the course of the SVP Switzerland under Christoph Blocher from the 1980s?
43581.e: The Zurich SVP under Blocher pushed through a national-conservative, oppositional course. As a result, the traditionally more moderate Bern wing lost influence.
43581.m: The Zurich wing around Blocher shaped the modern SVP.

43582.q: Who was president of the SVP Switzerland from 2008 to 2016?
43582.e: Toni Brunner from St Gallen succeeded Ueli Maurer in 2008. The party's record result came during his time in office.
43582.m: Toni Brunner led the SVP from 2008 to 2016.

43583.q: Which party names “overcoming capitalism” as a goal in its 2010 party programme?
43583.e: At its 2010 party conference in Lausanne, the SP adopted a new party programme. The wording about overcoming capitalism caused a great deal of debate.
43583.m: The SP adopted a new party programme in Lausanne in 2010.

43584.q: Which European policy goal does the SP's 2010 party programme set out?
43584.e: In its programme, the SP supports Switzerland joining the EU. This clearly sets it apart from the centre-right Federal Council parties.
43584.m: In its programme, the SP supports joining the EU.

43585.q: Who was president of the SP Switzerland from 2008 to 2020?
43585.e: Christian Levrat from Fribourg led the SP for twelve years. In 2020 a co-presidency took over.
43585.m: Christian Levrat was SP president from 2008 to 2020.

43586.q: Which SP politician lost the Federal Council election in 1983, although she was her party's official candidate?
43586.e: In 1983 the Federal Assembly elected the Social Democrat Otto Stich instead of Lilian Uchtenhagen. She would have been the first woman in the Federal Council.
43586.m: Lilian Uchtenhagen missed out on election to the Federal Council in 1983.

43587.q: How many seats has the SP had in the Council of States since the 2023 elections?
43587.e: In 2023 the SP held on to its 9 Council of States seats. This makes it the third strongest party in the smaller chamber.
43587.m: Since 2023 the SP has had nine members of the Council of States.

43588.q: As part of the labour movement, which association is the SP traditionally closely linked to?
43588.e: The SP and the trade unions both grew out of the labour movement of the 19th century. Many SP members of parliament hold posts in trade unions.
43588.m: The SP and the trade unions are closely linked.

43589.q: Which SP member of the Federal Council led the Department of Foreign Affairs from 2003 to 2011?
43589.e: Micheline Calmy-Rey from Geneva led the FDFA throughout her time in office. She coined the term active neutrality.
43589.m: Micheline Calmy-Rey was foreign minister from 2003 to 2011.

43590.q: Which slogan has shaped the SP Switzerland's election campaigns for years?
43590.e: The slogan “For all, not for the few” expresses the aim of a fairer distribution of wealth. The SP uses it on posters and in campaigns.
43590.m: The SP campaigns with the slogan “For all, not for the few”.

43591.q: Which three core values does the FDP name as the heart of its policy?
43591.e: The FDP bases its policy on the values of freedom, public spirit and progress. The freedom of the individual comes first.
43591.m: The FDP stands for freedom, public spirit and progress.

43592.q: How has the FDP's share of the vote in National Council elections developed since the early 1980s?
a: It fell clearly from over 20 per cent
It rose clearly to over 20 per cent
It always stayed about the same
43592.e: At the start of the 1980s the FDP still won over 20 per cent of the vote. Since then it has lost ground at almost every election, mainly to the SVP.
43592.m: The FDP's share of the vote has fallen sharply since the 1980s.

43593.q: Which party is the only one to have been represented in the Federal Council without a break since 1848?
43593.e: At first the Radicals provided all seven members of the Federal Council and have been in government ever since. The other parties joined only later.
43593.m: The FDP has been in the Federal Council without a break since 1848.

43594.q: Which Radical politician and businessman drove forward the building of the Gotthard railway in the 19th century?
43594.e: Alfred Escher founded, among other things, Credit Suisse (Schweizerische Kreditanstalt) and promoted railway building. He was a leading figure of business liberalism.
43594.m: Alfred Escher was the defining figure of business liberalism.

43595.q: Which basic economic policy stance shapes the FDP?
a: Economic liberalism with a free market
43595.e: The FDP favours a market economy, free trade and a lean state with low taxes. It is seen as the party of business.
43595.m: The FDP stands for economically liberal policies.

43596.q: Which political force pushed through the Federal Constitution of 1848 after the Sonderbund War?
43596.e: The victorious Liberals and Radicals founded the federal state in 1848. The FDP later emerged from this camp.
43596.m: The Radicals are seen as the founding party of the federal state.

43597.q: What share of the vote did the FDP achieve in the 2023 National Council elections?
43597.e: In 2023 the FDP lost about 0.8 percentage points and reached 14.3 per cent. It was its lowest figure so far.
43597.m: In 2023 the FDP won 14.3 per cent of the vote.

43598.q: Which FDP member of the Federal Council led the economics department from 2010 to 2018?
43598.e: Bernese businessman Johann Schneider-Ammann led the economics department throughout his time in office. Since 2013 it has been called the EAER.
43598.m: Johann Schneider-Ammann was economics minister from 2010 to 2018.

43599.q: Since what date has The Centre, the party formed by merging the CVP and BDP, officially existed?
43599.e: The delegates of both parties approved the merger in November 2020. It took effect on 1 January 2021.
43599.m: The Centre came into being on 1 January 2021.

43600.q: Which reference disappeared from the CVP's party name with the new name “The Centre”?
43600.e: By dropping the “C”, the party wanted to appeal to voters outside the Catholic milieu. The step was controversial within the party.
43600.m: With the name “The Centre”, the party dropped the “C”.

43601.q: Which member of the Federal Council belonged to the BDP from 2008 to 2015?
43601.e: Eveline Widmer-Schlumpf was elected in 2007 against the wishes of her SVP parliamentary group. She then moved to the newly founded BDP.
43601.m: Eveline Widmer-Schlumpf was the BDP's only member of the Federal Council.

43602.q: Which CVP member of the Federal Council led DETEC from 2010 and shaped the Energy Strategy 2050?
43602.e: After Fukushima in 2011, Doris Leuthard began the gradual phase-out of nuclear power. The people accepted the Energy Strategy 2050 in 2017.
43602.m: Doris Leuthard shaped the Energy Strategy 2050.

43603.q: In which 19th-century conflict did the Catholic Conservative camp form against the Radicals?
43603.e: In the Kulturkampf, the state and the Catholic Church fought over influence, for example in schools and marriage. This led to the political organisation of Catholics.
43603.m: The Kulturkampf shaped the Catholic Conservative camp.

43604.q: Which role is often attributed to The Centre in the polarised parliament?
a: It always votes with the SP
It always votes with the SVP
43604.e: Because neither the left nor the right bloc has a majority on its own, The Centre looks for partners depending on the issue. So it often decides which side wins.
43604.m: In Parliament, The Centre often tips the balance.

43605.q: In which canton was the first cantonal BDP founded in 2008, after the SVP Switzerland had expelled its section there?
43605.e: The Grisons SVP stood by its member of the Federal Council and was therefore expelled from the SVP Switzerland. It refounded itself as the BDP; Bern and Glarus followed.
43605.m: The BDP was founded first in the canton of Grisons in 2008.

43606.q: Who was president of the BDP when it merged with the CVP?
43606.e: Martin Landolt from Glarus led the BDP from 2012 until the merger. He supported joining with the CVP.
43606.m: Martin Landolt was the last president of the BDP.

43607.q: Where does The Centre, as successor to the CVP, traditionally have its strongholds?
a: In Catholic cantons such as Valais and Central Switzerland
In the big cities of the Central Plateau
In Protestant cantons such as Bern and Vaud
Mainly in the canton of Ticino
43607.e: The CVP has its roots in the Catholic Conservative milieu. That is why it is particularly strong in Central Switzerland and Valais.
43607.m: The Centre is traditionally strong in Catholic cantons.

43608.q: What share of the vote did the Greens achieve in the so-called climate election of 2019?
43608.e: In 2019 the Greens achieved their best result with 13.2 per cent. Climate strikes had put climate protection at the top of the agenda.
43608.m: In 2019 the Greens achieved their record result of 13.2 per cent.

43609.q: Which Green was the first member of her party to be president of the National Council, in 2012/13?
43609.e: Maya Graf from Basel-Landschaft presided over the National Council from November 2012 to November 2013. Irène Kälin followed as the second Green in 2021/22.
43609.m: Maya Graf was the first Green president of the National Council.

43610.q: Which Green stood unsuccessfully against Ignazio Cassis for the Federal Council in December 2019?
43610.e: Then party president Regula Rytz wanted to turn the election success into a Federal Council seat. However, the Federal Assembly re-elected Cassis.
43610.m: In 2019 Regula Rytz failed in her challenge for an FDP seat.

43611.q: Who was president of the Swiss Greens from 2020 to 2024?
43611.e: Zurich National Council member Balthasar Glättli succeeded Regula Rytz in 2020. In 2024 Lisa Mazzone took over.
43611.m: Balthasar Glättli led the Greens from 2020 to 2024.

43612.q: Which Green popular initiative called for fixed operating lives for nuclear power stations and was rejected in 2016?
43612.e: The initiative wanted to limit the operating life of nuclear power stations to 45 years. The people and the cantons rejected it in November 2016 with about 54 per cent voting no.
43612.m: The Greens' Nuclear Phase-Out Initiative failed in 2016.

43613.q: Which Green popular initiative called for an ecological footprint of only one Earth by 2050?
43613.e: The initiative “For a sustainable and resource-efficient economy” was put to the vote in September 2016. It was rejected with about 64 per cent voting no.
43613.m: The Green Economy initiative wanted to cut resource consumption sharply.

43614.q: In which year was the national umbrella organisation of the Greens founded in Fribourg?
43614.e: On 28 May 1983 the Federation of Green Parties of Switzerland was founded. Since 1986 it has been called the Green Party of Switzerland.
43614.m: The Green Party of Switzerland was founded in 1983.

43615.q: Which European party family do the Swiss Greens belong to?
a: The Alliance of Liberals and Democrats
43615.e: The Swiss Greens are members of the European Green Party. Green parties from all over Europe work together there.
43615.m: The Swiss Greens belong to the European Green Party.

43616.q: Why can the GLP form its own parliamentary group in the Federal Palace, but the EVP cannot?
a: Because a group needs at least five members
Because the EVP is not a Federal Council party
Because the EVP is only represented in the Council of States
Because groups are only open to green parties
43616.e: A parliamentary group needs at least five members from one of the two chambers. The GLP meets this; the EVP, with two seats, does not.
43616.m: A parliamentary group needs at least five members.

43617.q: With which principle does the GLP want to include environmental costs in prices?
43617.e: Those who harm the environment should pay for it. The GLP therefore relies on market-based incentive taxes rather than bans.
43617.m: The GLP relies on cost transparency through incentive taxes.

43618.q: Which GLP popular initiative was rejected in 2015 with about 92 per cent voting no?
43618.e: The initiative wanted to replace VAT with a tax on non-renewable energy. It suffered one of the clearest defeats in the history of Swiss votes.
43618.m: The GLP initiative Energy Tax instead of VAT failed clearly in 2015.

43619.q: Who was the first president of the GLP Switzerland, from 2007 to 2017?
43619.e: Martin Bäumle led the party from its founding until 2017. Then Jürg Grossen took over.
43619.m: Martin Bäumle was the first president of the GLP Switzerland.

43620.q: How many National Council seats did the GLP lose in the 2023 elections?
43620.e: In the National Council the GLP fell from 16 to 10 seats. In the Council of States, however, it won a seat for the first time.
43620.m: In 2023 the GLP lost six of its 16 National Council seats.

43621.q: How does the GLP position itself on social issues?
43621.e: The GLP supports, for example, marriage for all and a liberal drugs policy. It combines this stance with environmental protection and a market economy.
43621.m: The GLP is socially liberal and progressive.

43622.q: Where does the GLP typically achieve its best election results?
a: In the border regions of Ticino
43622.e: The GLP appeals mainly to well-educated, urban voters. In cities such as Zurich it is much stronger than in the countryside.
43622.m: The GLP is strongest in towns and cities.

43623.q: What share of the vote did the GLP achieve in the 2023 National Council elections?
43623.e: Compared with 2019, the GLP lost about 0.2 percentage points. It remained the sixth strongest party.
43623.m: In 2023 the GLP won 7.6 per cent of the vote.

43624.q: What does the abbreviation EDU stand for, the party to the right of the EVP?
43624.e: The EDU was founded in 1975 and holds strictly Christian conservative positions. Since 2023 it has had two seats in the National Council.
43624.m: EDU stands for Federal Democratic Union.

43625.q: How many National Council seats did the EVP lose in the 2023 elections?
43625.e: In 2023 the EVP fell from 3 to 2 seats. Its share of the vote fell slightly.
43625.m: In 2023 the EVP lost one of its three National Council seats.

43626.q: What share of the vote did the EVP achieve in the 2023 National Council elections?
43626.e: In 2023 the EVP won 2.0 per cent of the vote. This makes it the strongest of the small parties.
43626.m: In 2023 the EVP won about two per cent of the vote.

43627.q: Which popular initiative to tax large inheritances for AHV was rejected in 2015, after the EVP had played a key role in launching it?
43627.e: The initiative “Tax inheritances of millions for our AHV” wanted to tax estates of over 2 million francs. It was rejected in June 2015 with about 71 per cent voting no.
43627.m: The EVP helped launch an inheritance tax for AHV, which the people rejected in 2015.

43628.q: Which other Christian party stands clearly to the right of the EVP politically?
43628.e: The EDU holds strictly conservative positions and often works with the SVP. The EVP, by contrast, seeks solutions in the political centre.
43628.m: The EDU is on the right, the EVP in the centre.

43629.q: Where is the EVP usually placed on social and environmental issues?
a: Rather in the centre to centre-left
43629.e: The EVP campaigns for families, social welfare and protecting creation. On these issues it often votes with the centre-left.
43629.m: On social and environmental issues, the EVP tends towards the centre-left.

43630.q: In which cantons is the EVP traditionally strongest?
a: In Protestant cantons such as Zurich, Bern and Aargau
In Catholic cantons such as Uri and Valais
Mainly in the canton of Ticino
43630.e: The EVP has its roots in the Protestant Reformed milieu of German-speaking Switzerland. That is why it is strongest there.
43630.m: The EVP is rooted in the Protestant cantons of German-speaking Switzerland.

43631.q: In which year was the Lega dei Ticinesi founded?
43631.e: The Lega was founded in January 1991 as a protest party. In the same year it already won seats in the National Council.
43631.m: The Lega dei Ticinesi was founded in 1991.

43632.q: Which businessman founded the Lega dei Ticinesi together with the journalist Flavio Maspoli?
43632.e: Giuliano Bignasca was co-founder and long-time president of the Lega. He died in 2013.
43632.m: Giuliano Bignasca founded the Lega dei Ticinesi.

43633.q: What is the free Sunday newspaper published by the Lega dei Ticinesi called?
43633.e: The “Mattino della domenica” is the Lega's mouthpiece. The paper is known for its provocative style.
43633.m: The Lega spreads its messages in the “Mattino della domenica”.

43634.q: How many of the five seats in the Ticino cantonal government has the Lega held since 2011?
43634.e: Since 2011 the Lega has provided two of the five members of the Ticino government. It has been represented in the government since 1995.
43634.m: The Lega has two members of the Ticino government.

43635.q: Which parliamentary group does Lega National Council member Lorenzo Quadri belong to in the Federal Palace?
43635.e: With only one seat, the Lega cannot form its own group. Its representatives join the SVP group.
43635.m: In the Federal Palace, the Lega sits with the SVP group.

43636.q: Who has represented the Lega dei Ticinesi as its only member of the National Council since the 2023 elections?
43636.e: In 2023 the Lega won one of the eight Ticino National Council seats. It is held by Lorenzo Quadri, who has sat in the National Council since 2011.
43636.m: Lorenzo Quadri represents the Lega in the National Council.

43637.q: Which Lega politician was on the SVP's official three-person ticket for the Federal Council election in 2015?
43637.e: In 2015 the SVP proposed Thomas Aeschi, Guy Parmelin and Ticino cantonal minister Norman Gobbi. Guy Parmelin was elected.
43637.m: Norman Gobbi of the Lega was a Federal Council candidate in 2015.

43638.q: Which issue is particularly prominent for the Lega dei Ticinesi?
a: Protection against cross-border commuters and criticism of the EU
43638.e: The Lega criticises competition from Italian cross-border commuters on the Ticino job market. It also opposes joining the EU and criticises “Bern”.
43638.m: The Lega campaigns against competition from cross-border commuters and against the EU.

43639.q: Which Lega politician was mayor of Lugano from 2013 to 2021?
43639.e: Marco Borradori had previously been a cantonal minister for a long time and was seen as the moderate face of the Lega. He died in office in 2021.
43639.m: Marco Borradori led the city of Lugano as a Lega politician.

43640.q: With what percentage of no votes was the JUSO inheritance tax initiative rejected on 30 November 2025?
43640.e: The “Initiative for a Future” failed very clearly with 78.3 per cent voting no. Not a single canton approved it.
43640.m: The JUSO inheritance tax initiative failed clearly in 2025.

43641.q: What tax rate did the JUSO initiative “For a Future” demand on inheritances over 50 million francs?
43641.e: The revenue was to go to climate protection. Opponents warned that rich families might leave Switzerland as a result.
43641.m: JUSO wanted to tax very large inheritances at half their value.

43642.q: Which youth party launched the Urban Sprawl Initiative rejected in 2019?
43642.e: The initiative wanted to freeze building zones in Switzerland. It was rejected in February 2019 with about 64 per cent voting no.
43642.m: The Urban Sprawl Initiative came from the Young Greens.

43643.q: Which initiative against financing war material producers achieved a respectable 42.5 per cent yes in 2020?
43643.e: The initiative came from the GSoA and the Young Greens. Although it failed, it won a lot of yes votes for a youth party initiative.
43643.m: The War Business Initiative won over 40 per cent yes in 2020.

43644.q: Which JUSO initiative wanted to ban speculation on food and won 40.1 per cent yes in 2016?
43644.e: The initiative “No speculation on food” was rejected in February 2016. However, it won well over a third of the votes.
43644.m: With the Stop Speculation Initiative, JUSO wanted to ban speculation on food.

43645.q: Which current SP co-president led the JUSO Switzerland from 2008 to 2011?
43645.e: As JUSO president, Cédric Wermuth stood out with provocative actions. He later became a member of the National Council and in 2020 co-president of the SP.
43645.m: Cédric Wermuth was JUSO president before his SP career.

43646.q: Who took over as president of the JUSO Switzerland in 2024?
43646.e: Mirjam Hostetmann from Obwalden succeeded Nicola Siegrist in 2024. She led the party in the referendum campaign on the inheritance tax.
43646.m: Mirjam Hostetmann has been JUSO president since 2024.

43647.q: Which function do youth parties particularly often fulfil for their parent parties?
43647.e: Many well-known members of parliament gained their first experience in a youth party. Youth parties also often bring in sharper demands.
43647.m: Youth parties are a training ground for politics.

43648.q: Which criterion did the Italian philosopher Norberto Bobbio see as decisive for distinguishing left and right?
43648.e: In his book “Left and Right” (1994), Bobbio argued that the left places more emphasis on equality. The right tends to accept inequality as natural.
43648.m: According to Bobbio, the attitude to equality separates left and right.

43649.q: What does the so-called horseshoe theory say about the political spectrum?
a: The far ends resemble each other in some respects
The spectrum has only one axis
43649.e: According to the horseshoe theory, the extreme ends of the spectrum come close to each other, like the ends of a horseshoe. The theory is disputed in political science.
43649.m: The horseshoe theory sees similarities between the extreme ends.

43650.q: Which two parties form the left bloc in the National Council?
43650.e: The SP and the Greens vote together on most issues. Since 2023 they have had 64 seats together in the National Council.
43650.m: The SP and the Greens form the left bloc in Parliament.

43651.q: Which political geographer, with the research institute Sotomo, regularly places members of parliament on a left-right scale?
43651.e: Michael Hermann analyses how members of parliament vote. The so-called parliamentarian rating appears in the NZZ.
43651.m: Michael Hermann maps members of parliament on a political map.

43652.q: What does the abbreviation “TAN” stand for in the political science pair GAL-TAN?
43652.e: Hooghe and Marks contrast green-alternative-libertarian (GAL) positions with traditional-authoritarian-nationalist (TAN) ones. This axis adds to the economic left-right axis.
43652.m: The GAL-TAN scheme describes the cultural axis of conflict.

43653.q: Which parties are considered centre parties in the Swiss Parliament?
43653.e: The Centre, GLP and EVP lie between the left bloc and the right-wing parties. Depending on the issue, they form majorities with the left or the right.
43653.m: The Centre, GLP and EVP form the political centre.

43654.q: Which two axes does the well-known “Political Compass” use?
43654.e: The Political Compass adds a social axis to the economic one. It ranges from authoritarian to libertarian.
43654.m: The Political Compass places positions on two axes.

43655.q: What are positions on the far edge of the spectrum that reject the democratic constitutional state called?
43655.e: Extremist positions are directed against the foundations of democracy. Radical or populist positions do not necessarily do this.
43655.m: Extremism rejects the democratic constitutional state.

43656.q: Which development describes the polarisation of the Swiss party system since the 1990s?
a: The parties at the extremes gained, the centre lost
The number of parties fell to three
43656.e: Above all, the SVP on the right and the SP and Greens on the left gained ground. The FDP and CVP, by contrast, lost a lot of their share of the vote.
43656.m: Since the 1990s the extremes have grown stronger and the centre weaker.

43657.q: Which 1992 vote is seen as an important trigger for the rise of the SVP?
a: The vote on abolishing the army
The vote on joining the UN
43657.e: Under Blocher, the SVP campaigned almost alone among the Federal Council parties against joining the EEA, and won. After that, the European question became its main issue.
43657.m: The SVP's rise began with the no to the EEA in 1992.

43658.q: What is meant by affective polarisation?
a: Growing dislike of supporters of other parties
43658.e: Affective polarisation is about feelings towards political groups. Liking for your own group is set against dislike of the other.
43658.m: Affective polarisation describes feelings towards other parties.

43659.q: What do analyses of voting behaviour in the National Council since the 1990s show?
a: The parliamentary groups are further apart
All groups vote almost the same way
43659.e: Political geography analyses show that the groups have moved away from each other on the left-right axis. The centre has become narrower.
43659.m: The groups in the National Council have moved apart since the 1990s.

43660.q: What does the “effective number of parties” measure in political science?
a: How fragmented a party system is
How many parties sit in the Federal Council
How many members a party has
43660.e: The effective number of parties weights parties by their size. Switzerland has a high value compared with the rest of Europe.
43660.m: The effective number of parties measures how fragmented a party system is.

43661.q: What does the term voter volatility mean?
a: How much vote shares shift from election to election
How many parties stand for election
43661.e: High volatility means that many voters switch party. It is measured, for example, with the Pedersen index.
43661.m: Voter volatility shows how much vote shares shift.

43662.q: What combined share of the vote did the two parties at the extremes, SVP and SP, win in the 2023 National Council elections?
43662.e: The SVP won 27.9 per cent and the SP 18.3 per cent. Together that is about 46 per cent of the vote.
43662.m: In 2023 the SVP and SP together won almost half of the vote.

43663.q: Which new dividing line did the political scientist Hanspeter Kriesi see as the cause of polarisation in Western Europe?
a: Labour versus capital in the 19th century
Centre versus periphery in the Middle Ages
43663.e: Kriesi described the winners and losers of globalisation as the new poles. Parties such as the SVP mobilised the supporters of closure.
43663.m: Globalisation created a dividing line between openness and closure.

43664.q: On which smartspider axis does the FDP typically achieve a particularly high value?
43664.e: The FDP relies on the market, competition and little regulation. That is why it lies far out on the economic axis.
43664.m: In the smartspider, the FDP scores high on liberal economic policy.

43665.q: What does a value of 100 on an axis of the smartspider mean?
a: Full support for the axis's goal
Full rejection of the axis's goal
43665.e: Each axis runs from 0 to 100. The further out a point lies, the more strongly you support the goal named.
43665.m: The further out in the smartspider, the greater the support.

43666.q: Which of the following is an axis of the smartspider?
43666.e: The eight axes include open foreign policy, law and order and restrictive migration policy. Defence, education and transport are not separate axes.
43666.m: Restrictive migration policy is one of the eight smartspider axes.

43667.q: Which smartspider axis shows the attitude to international cooperation and the EU?
43667.e: Anyone supporting closer ties with the EU and international cooperation gets a high value. Opponents of opening up lie far in.
43667.m: The open foreign policy axis shows the attitude to the EU.

43668.q: Which smartspider axis covers the demand for harsher punishments and more police?
43668.e: The law and order axis measures support for a tough security and criminal justice policy. A high value means strong support.
43668.m: Harsher punishments show up in the smartspider on the law and order axis.

43669.q: How does smartvote calculate the match between voters and candidates?
a: Using the distance between the answer profiles
Using the number of party members
Using the age of the candidates
43669.e: The answers are treated as points in a space and the distance between them is calculated. smartvote used to use Euclidean distance for this; today it uses the city block model.
43669.m: smartvote measures the match by the distance between the answers.

a: Positions on a two-dimensional political map
The constituencies on a map of Switzerland
The seating plan in the National Council chamber
43670.e: The smartmap places candidates and parties on two axes. This shows who is politically close to whom.
43670.m: The smartmap is a two-dimensional political map.

43671.q: On which smartspider axis does the SVP typically achieve a particularly high value?
43671.e: The SVP campaigns for a strict immigration and asylum policy. On the welfare state, environmental protection and openness, it scores low.
43671.m: In the smartspider, the SVP scores high mainly on the migration axis.

43672.q: On which smartspider axis does the SP typically achieve a very high value?
43672.e: The SP calls for a strong welfare state with redistribution. On fiscal policy and law and order, by contrast, it lies far in.
43672.m: The SP has a high value for the welfare state in the smartspider.

43673.q: Which combination of high smartspider values fits the GLP best?
a: Expanded environmental protection and liberal society
Law and order and restrictive migration policy
Expanded welfare state and restrictive fiscal policy
Restrictive migration policy and expanded welfare state
43673.e: The GLP combines environmental concerns with socially liberal positions. That is why it lies far out on these two axes.
43673.m: In the smartspider, the GLP combines environmental protection and social openness.

43674.q: How many of the 23 cantonal votes were in favour of the EEA in 1992?
43674.e: Only 7 of 23 cantonal votes were in favour; the other 16 were against. The majority of the cantons was thus clearly missed.
43674.m: The EEA proposal failed clearly among the cantons.

43675.q: After the no to the EEA, which path did Switzerland choose to gain access to the EU single market?
a: A special status in the European Commission
A customs union with the EU
43675.e: Switzerland concluded sector-by-sector treaties with the EU in individual areas. This gave it access to parts of the single market without membership.
43675.m: After the no to the EEA, Switzerland chose the bilateral path.

43676.q: Which small state, which forms a customs union with Switzerland, joined the EEA in 1995?
43676.e: Liechtenstein voted for the EEA a week after Switzerland voted against it. Because of the customs treaty with Switzerland the agreement had to be adapted, and it joined on 1 May 1995.
43676.m: Liechtenstein is in the EEA, although Switzerland rejected it.

43677.q: The EEA links the EU with member states of which organisation, which Switzerland also belongs to?
43677.e: The EEA extends the EU single market to states of the European Free Trade Association. Switzerland has been a founding member of EFTA since 1960, but is not in the EEA.
43677.m: The EEA links the EU with most EFTA states.

43678.q: Besides Iceland and Liechtenstein, which country is today an EFTA member of the EEA?
43678.e: Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein are the three EFTA states in the EEA. Denmark, Austria and Sweden belong to the single market anyway as EU members.
43678.m: Switzerland is the only EFTA country outside the EEA.

43679.q: What is the divide between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland called, which was especially visible in the EEA vote?
43679.e: The term refers to rösti as a typical German-Swiss dish. It describes the different voting behaviour of the language regions.
43679.m: In some votes, the Röstigraben separates German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland.

43680.q: In which year did Switzerland and the EU sign the Bilateral Agreements I?
43680.e: After the no to the EEA, Switzerland negotiated for several years on seven sectoral agreements. They were signed in June 1999.
43680.m: The Bilaterals I were signed seven years after the no to the EEA.

43681.q: With what share of yes votes did the people accept the Bilateral Agreements I in May 2000?
43681.e: A referendum had been called against the Bilaterals I. The people clearly approved them, and they came into force in 2002.
43681.m: The Bilaterals I won a clear majority in 2000.

43682.q: What happened in 2016 to the application to join the EU that the Federal Council had submitted in 1992 before the EEA vote?
a: It was approved by the EU
It was turned into an EEA application
43682.e: After the no to the EEA, the application was on ice for decades. Following an instruction from Parliament, the Federal Council informed the EU in 2016 that it should be considered withdrawn.
43682.m: Switzerland's old application to join the EU has been withdrawn since 2016.

43683.q: What has the Federal Constitution banned since the Minaret Initiative was accepted in 2009?
a: The call to prayer by loudspeaker
43683.e: The initiative was accepted with 57.5 per cent voting yes. The ban is in Article 72 on church and state; mosques may still be built.
43683.m: Since 2009 the Constitution has banned the building of new minarets.

43684.q: What recommendation did the Federal Council and Parliament make on the Minaret Initiative?
43684.e: The Federal Council and Parliament recommended a no. The National Council rejected the initiative by 132 votes to 51, the Council of States by 39 to 3.
43684.m: The minaret ban was accepted against the recommendation of the Federal Council and Parliament.

43685.q: Which fundamental right did the Federal Council see as particularly threatened by the Minaret Initiative?
43685.e: The Federal Council warned that the initiative violated freedom of religion and conscience as well as equality before the law. It also saw religious peace at risk.
43685.m: The Federal Council saw the minaret ban as conflicting with freedom of religion.

43686.q: Politicians from which two parties formed the initiative committee of the Minaret Initiative?
43686.e: The committee had 16 members, 14 from the SVP and 2 from the EDU. It was led by Ulrich Schlüer, Walter Wobmann and Christian Waber.
43686.m: The Minaret Initiative came from SVP and EDU circles.

43687.q: Which federal extra-parliamentary commission criticised the Minaret Initiative's campaign poster as defamatory?
a: The Federal Commission for Child and Youth Affairs
43687.e: The poster showed minarets rising like missiles out of the Swiss flag. Several cities banned it from being displayed, which sparked a debate about freedom of expression.
43687.m: The Minaret Initiative poster caused a heated debate.

43688.q: Where was support for the Minaret Initiative particularly high in 2009?
43688.e: About 66 per cent voted yes in rural municipalities and about 54 per cent in urban ones. Only Basel-Stadt, Geneva, Neuchâtel and Vaud rejected it.
43688.m: In the Minaret Initiative, the countryside voted yes more clearly than the towns.

43690.q: Which other popular initiative from the same committee as the Minaret Initiative was accepted in 2021?
43690.e: The Egerkingen Committee also launched the initiative “Yes to a ban on face coverings”. It was accepted in March 2021 with 51.2% voting yes.
43690.m: In 2021 the committee behind the minaret ban also won the face-covering ban.

43691.q: Within what period did conflicting treaties have to be renegotiated under the Mass Immigration Initiative?
43691.e: The transitional provision required renegotiation within three years. This mainly affected the agreement on the free movement of persons with the EU.
43691.m: The initiative set a three-year deadline for renegotiation.

43692.q: Which measure to implement the Mass Immigration Initiative came into force on 1 July 2018?
a: The obligation to report job vacancies
Ending the free movement of persons
43692.e: Since then, vacancies in occupations with high unemployment must first be reported to the regional employment centres. This gives job seekers in Switzerland a head start.
43692.m: The obligation to report vacancies is the main implementation of the Mass Immigration Initiative.

43693.q: How did the people decide in 2020 on the Limitation Initiative, which called for ending the free movement of persons?
43693.e: The SVP's Limitation Initiative was clearly rejected in September 2020. If necessary, it would have required terminating the free movement agreement.
43693.m: The Limitation Initiative failed clearly in 2020.

43694.q: What was the official title of the 2020 Limitation Initiative?
43694.e: The SVP submitted the initiative in 2018. Unlike the Mass Immigration Initiative, it expressly called for ending the free movement of persons.
43694.m: The Limitation Initiative was officially called “For moderate immigration”.

43696.q: After the Mass Immigration Initiative, with which country was Switzerland unable for the time being to sign the negotiated protocol on free movement?
43696.e: Croatia had joined the EU in 2013, so free movement was to be extended to it. Switzerland only ratified the protocol in December 2016.
43696.m: Extending free movement to Croatia was delayed after 2014.

43697.q: In which large EU research programme was Switzerland's participation temporarily restricted after the Mass Immigration Initiative was accepted?
43697.e: The EU suspended negotiations on association with Horizon 2020. This was a noticeable setback for universities and research in Switzerland.
43697.m: After 2014 Switzerland's research cooperation with the EU suffered.

43698.q: How did the SVP react to the law implementing the Mass Immigration Initiative of December 2016?
a: It did not call a referendum
It lodged a complaint with the Federal Supreme Court
43698.e: The SVP sharply criticised the implementation as a breach of the Constitution. But it did not call a referendum, and later turned to the Limitation Initiative instead.
43698.m: No referendum was called against the implementation of the Mass Immigration Initiative.

43699.q: What is the clause called under which the other Bilateral I agreements also lapse if free movement of persons is terminated?
43699.e: The seven Bilateral I agreements are legally linked. If one lapses, all the others automatically cease to apply.
43699.m: Because of the guillotine clause, the Bilaterals I stand or fall together.

43700.q: What did the Deportation Initiative, accepted in 2010, call for?
a: Foreigners automatically lose their right of residence for certain crimes
All asylum seekers must leave Switzerland
Foreigners may no longer be naturalised
Immigration from the EU is stopped
43700.e: The SVP initiative called for foreigners to be expelled after certain crimes. The people and the cantons narrowly accepted it in November 2010.
43700.m: The Deportation Initiative calls for criminal foreigners to be expelled.

43701.q: How did the direct counter-proposal to the Deportation Initiative fare?
a: It was rejected by the people and all the cantons
It was accepted and replaced the initiative
It was accepted only by the people
It was withdrawn before the vote
43701.e: The counter-proposal won neither a majority of the people nor a single canton. It would have linked deportation to the severity of the sentence and expressly respected international law.
43701.m: The counter-proposal to the Deportation Initiative failed completely.

43702.q: In which law was expulsion written to implement the Deportation Initiative?
43702.e: Parliament added Article 66a on mandatory expulsion to the Criminal Code. A criminal court orders it together with the judgment.
43702.m: Expulsion is set out in the Criminal Code.

43703.q: Who orders a mandatory expulsion in Switzerland?
43703.e: Expulsion is set out in the Criminal Code. The criminal court orders it together with the judgment against the convicted person.
43703.m: A criminal court decides on expulsion.

43704.q: Which provision allows courts, in exceptional cases, not to order an expulsion?
43704.e: The court can decide not to expel if this would cause serious personal hardship. In addition, private interests must outweigh public ones.
43704.m: The hardship clause allows exceptions to expulsion.

43705.q: What happened to the SVP's Enforcement Initiative on 28 February 2016?
a: It was rejected by the people and the cantons
43705.e: The Enforcement Initiative wanted to implement the Deportation Initiative directly without exceptions. About 59% of voters rejected it, with turnout over 63%.
43705.m: The Enforcement Initiative failed at the ballot box in 2016.

43706.q: What must Parliament do if a popular initiative is accepted that cannot be applied directly?
a: Submit the initiative to the Federal Supreme Court
43706.e: Many initiatives only change the Constitution and then need a law to set out the details. For the Deportation Initiative this took until 2016.
43706.m: Accepted initiatives often need an implementing law.

43707.q: Which SVP popular initiative wanted to implement the Deportation Initiative without exceptions in 2016?
43707.e: The Enforcement Initiative wanted to write a list of offences directly into the Constitution, without a hardship clause. The people and the cantons rejected it in February 2016.

43708.q: How clearly did the people reject joining the UN in the first vote in 1986?
43708.e: In 1986 three quarters of voters and all the cantons rejected joining. At that time many saw membership as incompatible with neutrality.
43708.m: The first attempt to join the UN failed very clearly in 1986.

43709.q: What was unique in the world about Switzerland joining the UN?
a: Membership was decided by a popular vote
Switzerland immediately got a permanent seat on the Security Council
43709.e: Switzerland is the first country to join the UN as a result of a popular vote. In other countries the government or parliament decided.
43709.m: Switzerland was the first country to join the UN by popular vote.

43710.q: Which canton had the highest share of yes votes for joining the UN in 2002?
43710.e: Geneva voted yes most clearly, with 66.9%. With the Palais des Nations, the city is home to the UN's European headquarters.
43710.m: Geneva, as a UN location, said yes to joining most clearly.

43711.q: Which canton rejected joining the UN most clearly in 2002, with 67.5% voting no?
43711.e: The rural cantons of Central and Eastern Switzerland were sceptical. The no was strongest in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
43711.m: Joining the UN met resistance in rural cantons.

43712.q: How did the second vote on Switzerland joining the UN come about in 2002?
a: Through a Federal Supreme Court ruling
Through a demand from the UN
Through a decision of the cantonal governments
43712.e: After the clear no of 1986, a cross-party committee launched a popular initiative in 1998. It was accepted by the people and the cantons in 2002.
43712.m: The second attempt to join the UN began with a popular initiative.

43713.q: When did Switzerland formally become a UN member after the popular vote of March 2002?
a: On the day of the vote in March 2002
43713.e: A few months after the popular vote, the UN General Assembly in New York admitted Switzerland on 10 September 2002.
43713.m: Switzerland has been a UN member since September 2002.

43714.q: What status did Switzerland already have at the UN before becoming a full member in 2002?
43714.e: Switzerland had been an observer at the UN since 1948 and a member of many specialised agencies. But it could not vote in the General Assembly.
43714.m: Before 2002 Switzerland was only an observer at the UN.

43715.q: Which concern was a main reason for the no to joining the UN in 1986?
a: The obligation to introduce the euro
The loss of the national languages
43715.e: In 1986 a majority considered membership incompatible with neutrality. By 2002 only about 28 per cent still held this view.
43715.m: By 2002 far fewer people saw a conflict between the UN and neutrality.

43716.q: What share of voters said yes to abolishing the army in 1989?
43716.e: Exactly 35.6 per cent said yes. The result was far above the expectations of the Federal Council and of those who launched the initiative.
43716.m: In 1989 over a third of voters wanted to abolish the army.

43717.q: Which writer supported the initiative to abolish the army in 1989 and wrote “Switzerland without an army? A palaver” about it?
43717.e: Max Frisch, like Friedrich Dürrenmatt, publicly supported the initiative. His text appeared in 1989 as a dialogue about the army.
43717.m: In 1989 Max Frisch supported the initiative for a Switzerland without an army.

43718.q: How did the GSoA's second initiative to abolish the army fare in 2001?
a: It did not get enough signatures
43718.e: In December 2001 about 78% rejected the initiative. The result was well below that of 1989.
43718.m: The second attempt to abolish the army failed clearly in 2001.

43719.q: What was Parliament's position on the initiative to abolish the army?
a: It put forward a direct counter-proposal
43719.e: The National Council rejected it by 172 votes to 13, and the Council of States even unanimously. There was no counter-proposal.
43719.m: Abolishing the army had hardly any support in Parliament.

43720.q: According to a post-vote survey, which age group mostly voted to abolish the army in 1989?
43720.e: The 20 to 30-year-olds said yes by about three to two. The over-60s, by contrast, rejected the initiative very clearly.
43720.m: The 1989 army vote showed a strong generation gap.

43721.q: In which year was the Group for a Switzerland without an Army (GSoA) founded?
43721.e: The GSoA was founded at the start of the 1980s in the context of the peace movement. A few years later it launched its first popular initiative.

43722.q: According to a post-vote survey, supporters of which party had a yes majority for abolishing the army in 1989?
43722.e: Among the SP, the Greens and other left-wing parties there were yes majorities. SVP and FDP supporters, by contrast, rejected it by about 91 per cent.
43722.m: The 1989 army vote clearly divided the parties.

43723.q: With which principle did the Federal Council justify rejecting the initiative to abolish the army?
43723.e: Switzerland sees itself as a neutral state that can protect its neutrality by military means. Without an army, the Federal Council saw this principle called into question.
43723.m: In 1989 the Federal Council defended armed neutrality.

43724.q: Who was allowed to vote on the Schwarzenbach Initiative at federal level in 1970?
43724.e: Women's suffrage at federal level was only introduced in February 1971. So in 1970 only men voted, then from the age of 20.
43724.m: Only men decided on the Schwarzenbach Initiative.

43725.q: What was the official title of the Schwarzenbach Initiative?
43725.e: The initiative went down in history as the second initiative against foreign infiltration (Überfremdung). It is usually named after the man who launched it.
43725.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative was officially the initiative against foreign infiltration.

43726.q: Who is the 1970 initiative against foreign infiltration usually named after?
a: The man who launched it, James Schwarzenbach
The then President of the Confederation
The place where signatures were collected
43726.e: Zurich National Council member James Schwarzenbach launched the initiative. That is why people still speak of the Schwarzenbach Initiative today.
43726.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative bears the name of the man who launched it.

43727.q: What, in essence, did the 1970 Schwarzenbach Initiative call for?
a: A sharp reduction in the share of foreigners
43727.e: The share of foreigners would have had to fall to at most 10% in almost every canton. Hundreds of thousands would have had to leave Switzerland.
43727.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative wanted to cut the share of foreigners sharply.

43728.q: What was the result of the vote on the Schwarzenbach Initiative in 1970?
43728.e: The initiative failed with about 54% voting no. Turnout was exceptionally high at about 75%.
43728.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative failed only narrowly in 1970.

43729.q: According to the 1970 census, roughly what was the share of foreigners in the Swiss resident population?
43729.e: Since the Second World War, the share had risen sharply because of the strong demand for workers. This development formed the background to the debate on foreign infiltration.
43729.m: Around 1970 far more foreigners lived in Switzerland than after the war.

43730.q: Around 1970, which country did the largest group of foreigners in Switzerland come from?
43730.e: Many Italians worked as seasonal workers or annual residents in construction and industry. They were particularly affected by the initiative.
43730.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative mainly affected Italian workers.

43731.q: Which group of the population supported the Schwarzenbach Initiative particularly strongly?
a: Business owners in the export industry
Civil servants in the federal administration
43731.e: Support was highest, for example, in working-class districts of Zurich and Basel. Many feared competition for jobs and housing.
43731.m: The Schwarzenbach Initiative found support mainly in working-class districts.

43732.q: How many valid signatures does a federal popular initiative need today?
43732.e: Since 1977, 100,000 signatures within 18 months have been needed. At the time of the Schwarzenbach Initiative it was still 50,000.
43732.m: A popular initiative today needs 100,000 signatures.

43733.q: Which former Ticino member of the Council of States was co-president of the initiative committee of the Responsible Business Initiative?
43733.e: FDP politician and former public prosecutor Dick Marty shaped the campaign as its centre-right face. He was known internationally for his investigations for the Council of Europe.
43733.m: Dick Marty was a prominent face of the Responsible Business Initiative.

43734.q: Why did the Responsible Business Initiative fail in November 2020?
a: It did not win a majority of the cantons
It did not win a majority of the people
43734.e: About 50.7 per cent of voters said yes, but the majority of the cantons rejected it. A popular initiative needs a majority of both the people and the cantons.
43734.m: Despite a majority of the people, the Responsible Business Initiative failed for lack of a majority of the cantons.

43735.q: What was the official title of the Responsible Business Initiative?
a: “For responsible businesses, protecting people and the environment”
“For a ban on financing war material producers”
43735.e: The title stresses the protection of people and the environment. In everyday speech, people almost only spoke of the Responsible Business Initiative.
43735.m: The Responsible Business Initiative called for responsible businesses.

43736.q: Which other popular initiative was rejected on the same day as the Responsible Business Initiative?
43736.e: The initiative against financing war material producers won about 42.5% yes. It failed to win a majority of the people or the cantons.
43736.m: The War Business Initiative also failed on the same day.

43737.q: What happened after the no to the Responsible Business Initiative in November 2020?
a: Parliament's indirect counter-proposal came into force
The vote was repeated because of irregularities
The Federal Council implemented the initiative anyway
The Federal Supreme Court declared the result invalid
43737.e: Because the initiative failed to win a majority of the cantons, the indirect counter-proposal automatically came into force. It has applied since 1 January 2022 and mainly requires reports and due diligence checks.
43737.m: After the no to the Responsible Business Initiative, the counter-proposal came into force.

43738.q: For which two areas does the counter-proposal to the Responsible Business Initiative lay down special due diligence obligations?
43738.e: Companies must check the risks in their supply chain in these areas. However, the counter-proposal does not provide for liability for damage abroad.
43738.m: The counter-proposal requires due diligence on conflict minerals and child labour.

43739.q: For which companies did the Responsible Business Initiative provide relief?
43739.e: Small and medium-sized enterprises were only to be affected if they worked in high-risk areas. This was meant to keep the burden on small businesses low.
43739.m: The Responsible Business Initiative wanted to spare SMEs with low risks.

43740.q: What is the minimum number of the 23 cantonal votes a popular initiative needs for a majority of the cantons?
43740.e: A majority of the cantonal votes is required, so more than 11½. In a tie of 11½ to 11½, there is no majority of the cantons.
43740.m: A majority of the cantons needs at least 12 cantonal votes.

43741.q: Which popular right made the votes on the Covid-19 Act possible?
43741.e: An optional referendum can be called against federal laws. It requires 50,000 signatures within 100 days.
43741.m: A referendum against a federal law needs 50,000 signatures.

43742.q: How many times did the Swiss people vote on the Covid-19 Act?
43742.e: The people voted on the law or its amendments in June 2021, November 2021 and June 2023. Each time a majority said yes.
43742.m: There were three votes on the Covid-19 Act.

43743.q: In which month did Parliament pass the Covid-19 Act?
43743.e: The law was passed on 25 September 2020. It turned the Federal Council's emergency ordinances from spring 2020 into a regular law.
43743.m: The Covid-19 Act was passed in autumn 2020.

43744.q: What was particularly controversial in the November 2021 vote on the Covid-19 Act?
a: The legal basis for the Covid certificate
43744.e: Among other things, the amendment provided the basis for the Covid certificate. Turnout was very high at about 65 per cent.
43744.m: In November 2021 the vote was mainly about the Covid certificate.

43745.q: Which youth movement campaigned against the Covid-19 Act?
43745.e: MASS-VOLL emerged during the pandemic out of protest against the measures. The movement supported the referendums against the law.
43745.m: MASS-VOLL was among the opponents of the Covid-19 Act.

43746.q: Until when were some provisions of the Covid-19 Act extended by the June 2023 vote?
43746.e: Parliament had extended some provisions as a precaution until June 2024. After that, the law largely expired.
43746.m: The Covid-19 Act largely expired in mid-2024.

43747.q: Among other things, which support did the Covid-19 Act voted on in June 2021 regulate?
a: Free public transport for nursing staff
43747.e: The law formed the basis for hardship aid, income compensation and short-time work compensation. This aid was the main focus of the first vote.
43747.m: The Covid-19 Act secured aid for businesses affected.

43748.q: Besides the Covid-19 Act, which law, accepted by the people in 2013, formed the basis for the pandemic measures?
43748.e: The revised Epidemics Act distinguishes between a normal, a special and an extraordinary situation. The Federal Council based its measures on it from 2020.
43748.m: The Epidemics Act sets out when the Confederation takes charge during epidemics.

43749.q: What was the result of the vote on the 13th AHV pension in March 2024?
a: Accepted with about 58% yes and a majority of the cantons
Accepted by the people, but failed the majority of the cantons
43749.e: Almost six out of ten voters said yes. The majority of the cantons also agreed.
43749.m: The 13th AHV pension won a clear majority.

43750.q: What made the acceptance of the 13th AHV pension historically special?
a: For the first time, the people accepted a left-wing initiative to expand the welfare state
For the first time, Swiss abroad voted electronically
For the first time, an initiative was valid without a majority of the cantons
43750.e: Until 2024, all popular initiatives to expand social insurance had failed. The proposal also found support among parts of the centre-right grassroots.
43750.m: The 13th AHV pension was the first left-wing social initiative to be accepted.

43751.q: What did the Pensions Initiative call for, which was clearly rejected on the same day as the 13th AHV pension?
a: A higher retirement age, linked to life expectancy
43751.e: The Young Liberals' proposal wanted to raise the retirement age to 66 and then link it to life expectancy. About three quarters of voters and all the cantons rejected it.
43751.m: The Pensions Initiative failed very clearly in 2024.

43752.q: A person receives a monthly AHV pension of 2000 francs. How much is their annual AHV pension with the 13th pension?
43752.e: With the 13th pension, there are 13 instead of 12 monthly payments a year. 13 times 2000 francs is 26,000 francs.
43752.m: The 13th AHV pension adds one extra monthly payment a year.

43753.q: Roughly by what percentage does the 13th pension increase the annual AHV pension?
43753.e: One extra monthly payment on top of the previous twelve equals 1 divided by 12, so about 8.3%. The initiative called for exactly this supplement.
43753.m: The 13th pension increases the annual pension by one twelfth.

43754.q: From which year is the 13th AHV pension paid for the first time?
43754.e: The initiative required payment from the second year after acceptance at the latest. It is paid each December.
43754.m: From 2026 the 13th AHV pension is paid every December.

43755.q: What was the official title of the initiative for a 13th AHV pension?
a: “For a better life in old age”
43755.e: The initiative focused on pensioners' loss of purchasing power. It called for a supplement equal to one extra monthly pension.
43755.m: The 13th AHV pension came with the initiative “For a better life in old age”.

43756.q: Which trade union president shaped the campaign for the 13th AHV pension?
43756.e: Pierre-Yves Maillard is president of the Swiss Trade Union Federation. He put pensioners' purchasing power at the centre of the campaign.
43756.m: Pierre-Yves Maillard was the face of the campaign for the 13th AHV pension.

43757.q: What does the Alpine Initiative, now part of the Federal Constitution, call for?
a: Freight traffic across the Alps should move from road to rail
All Alpine passes should be closed in winter
No new ski areas should be built in the Alps
Lorries should cross the Alps for free
43757.e: The article “Transalpine transit traffic” protects the Alpine region from the effects of transit traffic. Freight from border to border is to go by rail.
43757.m: The Alpine Initiative aims to put transit freight on the railways.

43758.q: Which canton approved the Alpine Initiative most clearly, with about 87.6%?
43758.e: Uri lies on the Gotthard route and suffers particularly from lorry traffic. The other Gotthard cantons also clearly voted yes.
43758.m: The Gotthard canton of Uri said yes to the Alpine Initiative most clearly.

43759.q: How many lorry journeys across the Alps per year did the law set as the transfer target?
43759.e: The Goods Traffic Transfer Act set a target of at most 650,000 journeys a year. It was to be reached two years after the Gotthard Base Tunnel opened, but was missed.
43759.m: The transfer target is 650,000 lorry journeys a year.

43760.q: Which charge did Switzerland introduce in 2001 to encourage moving freight onto the railways?
a: The CO2 levy on heating oil
43760.e: The LSVA charges lorries according to the kilometres driven, their weight and emission standard. Part of the revenue funds the expansion of the railway infrastructure.
43760.m: The LSVA makes lorry journeys more expensive and so encourages rail.

43761.q: Which canton rejected the Alpine Initiative most clearly in 1994?
43761.e: In Valais, 74.4% voted no. Many feared disadvantages for their own transport links.
43761.m: Valais was the strongest opponent of the Alpine Initiative.

43762.q: Which German-speaking Swiss canton was the only one to reject the Alpine Initiative in 1994?
43762.e: All the other German-speaking cantons voted yes. Otherwise, the no came mainly from French-speaking Switzerland.
43762.m: Almost all of German-speaking Switzerland approved the Alpine Initiative.

43763.q: Which debate at the end of the 1980s led to the Alpine Initiative being launched?
a: The building of the Gotthard road tunnel
The introduction of the motorway vignette
43763.e: Environmental groups from several mountain regions launched the initiative in 1989. They feared more lorry traffic through the Alps if heavier lorries were allowed.
43763.m: Fear of heavier lorries led to the Alpine Initiative.

43764.q: Which international agreement did the Federal Council cite as a reason why the Alpine Initiative was not needed?
43764.e: The Federal Council referred to the Alpine Convention as well as to Rail 2000 and the NRLA. It preferred an overall transport policy without compulsion.
43764.m: In 1994 the Federal Council referred to the Alpine Convention.

43765.q: Since the Second Homes Initiative, what maximum share of second homes per municipality does the Federal Constitution set?
43765.e: Article 75b of the Constitution limits the share of second homes to a maximum of 20 per cent. Municipalities above this can hardly approve any new second homes.
43765.m: A municipality may have at most 20 per cent second homes.

43766.q: By which nickname is the Second Homes Initiative known?
43766.e: The nickname comes from the man who launched it. It should not be confused with the Lex Koller, which regulates the purchase of property by people abroad.
43766.m: The Second Homes Initiative is often called the Lex Weber.

43767.q: Which committee submitted the Second Homes Initiative?
43767.e: Helvetia Nostra is part of the circle of the Franz Weber Foundation. The initiative was supported by other environmental organisations.
43767.m: The Second Homes Initiative came from Helvetia Nostra.

43768.q: What does the permitted maximum share of second homes in a municipality refer to?
a: The total stock of homes and the gross floor area
43768.e: What counts is the share of the municipality's total housing stock and living space. If the limit is exceeded, strict building restrictions apply.
43768.m: The second homes limit is measured against a municipality's housing stock.

43769.q: What regulated second homes between the 2012 vote and the law coming into force?
a: A Federal Supreme Court ruling alone
43769.e: The Federal Council issued a transitional ordinance so that the new constitutional article could be applied immediately. Later the Second Homes Act replaced this ordinance.
43769.m: Until the Second Homes Act, a Federal Council ordinance applied.

43770.q: Which new homes may still be built under certain conditions in municipalities with too many second homes?
a: Homes for weekly residents from abroad
43770.e: Homes that are permanently offered for short-term rental to guests are allowed. They are meant to strengthen tourism without creating “cold beds”.
43770.m: Homes rented to tourists are possible despite the second homes limit.

43771.q: What recommendation did the Federal Council and Parliament make on the Second Homes Initiative?
43771.e: The Federal Council and Parliament recommended a no and referred to the revised Spatial Planning Act. The initiative was accepted anyway.
43771.m: The Second Homes Initiative was accepted against the authorities' advice.

43772.q: What must municipalities draw up every year under the Second Homes Act?
a: A list of all hotel guests
43772.e: The inventory of homes shows a municipality's share of second homes. If it is above the limit, the restrictions apply.
43772.m: An annual inventory of homes shows a municipality's share of second homes.

43773.q: In which year was Economiesuisse created through a merger?
43773.e: Economiesuisse was created in 2000 from the merger of the Vorort and the Society for the Promotion of the Swiss Economy (wf). The Vorort itself dated back to 1870.
43773.m: Economiesuisse has existed in its current form since 2000.

43774.q: Which long-established organisation became part of Economiesuisse in 2000?
43774.e: The Vorort, officially the Swiss Trade and Industry Association, was the leading business association of the 19th and 20th centuries. In 2000 it merged with the wf to form Economiesuisse.
43774.m: The Vorort is the most important predecessor of Economiesuisse.

43775.q: What kind of organisation does Economiesuisse see itself as?
a: Umbrella organisation of the Swiss economy
43775.e: Economiesuisse is the umbrella organisation of the Swiss economy. It represents industry associations and chambers of commerce towards politics and the public.
43775.m: Economiesuisse is an umbrella organisation, not a party.

43776.q: Who are typically the members of Economiesuisse?
a: Industry associations and cantonal chambers of commerce
Federal Council parties and youth parties
43776.e: The members of Economiesuisse are mainly industry associations, for example from manufacturing, finance or pharmaceuticals, as well as cantonal chambers of commerce. Individual companies can also be members.
43776.m: Economiesuisse brings together the voices of many industry associations and chambers of commerce.

43777.q: In which city does Economiesuisse have its headquarters?
43777.e: Economiesuisse's headquarters are in Zurich, where the Vorort was also based. It also has offices in Bern, Geneva and Lugano, among other places.
43777.m: Economiesuisse has its headquarters in Zurich.

43778.q: Which popular initiative was accepted in 2013 with about 68% yes, despite an expensive counter-campaign by Economiesuisse?
43778.e: Thomas Minder's Rip-Off Initiative (against excessive executive pay) was accepted on 3 March 2013 with 67.9% voting yes. Economiesuisse had run an elaborate no campaign.
43778.m: Even an expensive campaign does not guarantee winning a vote.

43779.q: In which particularly visible way does Economiesuisse influence direct democracy?
a: Through its own seats in the Federal Council
Through a right to veto laws
43779.e: Economiesuisse often runs or funds campaigns on economic policy proposals. The association has no formal right to share in state decisions.
43779.m: Business associations influence popular votes mainly through campaigns.

43780.q: Besides the Vorort, which business organisation was involved in founding Economiesuisse?
a: The wf (Society for the Promotion of the Swiss Economy)
43780.e: The wf was mainly responsible for public relations and information. In 2000 it merged with the Vorort, which handled lobbying, to form Economiesuisse.
43780.m: Economiesuisse combines the Vorort's former lobbying with the wf's communication work.

43782.q: Which trade union has the most members in the Swiss Trade Union Federation?
43782.e: Unia is the largest trade union in Switzerland and a member of the SGB. It mainly organises workers in construction, industry, trades and private services.
43782.m: Unia is the largest member union of the SGB.

a: Workers stopping work together to push through demands
An advertising campaign by a trade union
43783.e: In a strike, workers stop working, usually when called on by a trade union such as Unia. In Switzerland strikes are fairly rare thanks to social partnership.
43783.m: A strike is a collective stoppage of work.

43784.q: Which popular initiative launched by the SGB was accepted on 3 March 2024?
43784.e: The initiative “For a better life in old age” called for a 13th monthly AHV pension. It was accepted by the people and the cantons on 3 March 2024, which was unusual for a trade union initiative.
43784.m: With the 13th AHV pension, the Trade Union Federation won a popular vote in 2024.

43785.q: How did the trade unions' Minimum Wage Initiative fare at the ballot box in 2014?
43785.e: The initiative called for a national minimum wage of 22 francs an hour. It was rejected in May 2014 by about 76 per cent of voters.
43785.m: A national minimum wage failed clearly at the ballot box in 2014.

43786.q: Which group does the SGB, as an umbrella organisation, mainly represent?
43786.e: The SGB is the largest umbrella organisation of employees in Switzerland. It represents the concerns of its member unions towards politics and employers.
43786.m: The Trade Union Federation represents the interests of employees.

43787.q: Which party is the SGB traditionally particularly close to?
43787.e: Historically, the SGB is close to social democracy. Many of its leading figures sit in the Federal Parliament for the SP.
43787.m: The SGB is traditionally close to social democracy.

43788.q: Which trade union in the SGB mainly organises public sector staff?
43788.e: The VPOD (Swiss Union of Public Service Personnel) represents employees of the Confederation, cantons, municipalities and public enterprises. The SEV, by contrast, mainly organises transport staff.
43788.m: The VPOD is the union of public sector staff.

43789.q: What role does the Swiss Farmers' Union (SBV) have?
a: It is the umbrella organisation of Swiss agriculture
It is the federal agriculture office
It is a farmers' party in Parliament
It is a cooperative for farm machinery
43789.e: The Swiss Farmers' Union represents farming families towards politics and the public. It has existed since 1897.
43789.m: The Swiss Farmers' Union is the umbrella organisation of agriculture.

43790.q: In which Aargau town does the Swiss Farmers' Union have its headquarters?
43790.e: The SBV has its headquarters on Laurstrasse in Brugg in the canton of Aargau. The street is named after the first farmers' secretary.
43790.m: The Farmers' Union has its headquarters in Brugg.

43791.q: Which farmers' politician co-founded the Farmers' Party in Bern in 1918, from which the SVP later emerged?
43791.e: Rudolf Minger co-founded the Farmers', Trades' and Citizens' Party. In 1929 he became its first member of the Federal Council, and in 1971 the SVP emerged from the BGB.
43791.m: The SVP later emerged from the farmers' party BGB.

43792.q: Why is the farming lobby considered particularly influential in the Federal Parliament?
a: Many members are themselves farmers or association representatives
It has a legal veto on agricultural questions
It is guaranteed a Federal Council seat by the Constitution
It elects the members of the agriculture committees
43792.e: Compared with agriculture's small share of the population, many farmers and association officials sit in Parliament. There is no formal right of veto.
43792.m: The farming lobby is strong because agriculture is over-represented in Parliament.

43793.q: What are direct payments in Swiss agriculture?
a: Federal contributions to farms for certain services
Cash payments when selling at the market
Payments by farmers to the Confederation
43793.e: The Confederation pays farms contributions, for example for landscape care, animal welfare or biodiversity. They make up an important part of farm income.
43793.m: Direct payments reward farmers for services to the public.

43794.q: Who are the members of the Swiss Farmers' Union?
a: Cantonal farmers' associations and specialist organisations
43794.e: The SBV is an umbrella organisation. Its members are the cantonal farmers' associations as well as specialist and producer organisations, for example of milk or vegetable producers.
43794.m: The Farmers' Union is an umbrella organisation of cantonal and specialist organisations.

43795.q: Which event takes place every year on many farms on the national holiday?
a: The cattle coming down from the Alps
43795.e: On 1 August, many farms invite people to brunch on the farm. The idea is to bring the public and agriculture closer together.
43795.m: The 1 August brunch brings the public onto the farms.

43796.q: Which main aim does the Farmers' Union typically pursue in agricultural policy?
a: Securing direct payments and border protection
Lowering food prices to EU levels
43796.e: The SBV campaigns for a sufficient agricultural budget with direct payments and for protecting domestic production from cheap imports. This secures farming families' income.
43796.m: The Farmers' Union fights for direct payments and border protection.

43797.q: In response to which development did employers' associations emerge at the start of the 20th century?
a: The growing strength of the trade unions
The founding of the federal state
43797.e: The forerunner of the Swiss Employers' Association was founded in 1908. Employers wanted to face the ever stronger trade unions united.
43797.m: Employers' associations emerged as a counterpart to the trade unions.

43798.q: Which policy areas does the Swiss Employers' Association focus on?
a: Labour market, education and social policy
43798.e: The Employers' Association is the voice of employers on questions of the labour market, social insurance and vocational training. It is thus the counterpart to the trade unions.
43798.m: The Employers' Association represents employers on the labour market and social policy.

43799.q: At which international organisation does the Employers' Association represent Swiss employers?
43799.e: The ILO, based in Geneva, is made up of three parts: governments, employers and workers. Swiss employers are represented there by the Employers' Association.
43799.m: In the International Labour Organization, states, employers and workers sit together.

43800.q: In which city is the Swiss Employers' Association based?
43800.e: The Swiss Employers' Association is based in Zurich. Until 1996 it was called the Central Association of Swiss Employers' Organisations.
43800.m: The Employers' Association is based in Zurich.

43801.q: Who are the members of the Swiss Employers' Association?
43801.e: The Employers' Association is an umbrella organisation of industry associations, regional employers' organisations and some individual firms. Together they represent a large share of the workforce.
43801.m: The Employers' Association mainly brings together employers' organisations.

43802.q: On which social insurance question does the Employers' Association regularly act as an important player?
a: Reform of retirement provision (AHV and BVG)
43802.e: Retirement provision is largely funded by contributions from wages, which employers share. That is why the Employers' Association is heavily involved in AHV and BVG reforms.
43802.m: Employers contribute to AHV and pension funds and therefore have a say in reforms.

43803.q: What is the basic principle under which employers' and employees' associations negotiate working conditions themselves called?
43803.e: In social partnership, employers' and employees' organisations largely regulate wages and working conditions themselves, mostly in collective labour agreements. The state only steps in to complement them.
43803.m: In social partnership, employers and trade unions negotiate directly with each other.

43804.q: What position does the Employers' Association typically take on statutory minimum wages?
43804.e: The Employers' Association argues that wages should be set through social partnership and not by the state. That is why it fought the 2014 Minimum Wage Initiative, for example.
43804.m: Employers prefer to set wages through social partnership rather than by law.

43805.q: Which companies does the Swiss Trade Association (SGV) mainly represent?
43805.e: The SGV is the umbrella organisation of Swiss SMEs. SMEs make up over 99 per cent of Swiss companies.
43805.m: The Trade Association is the voice of SMEs.
